60.h: 56 - Saʿd ibn Muʿādh ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Imriʾ al-Qays al-Anṣārī *
60.t:
Ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal.
The great chief, the martyr, Abū ʿAmr al-Anṣārī, al-Awsī, al-Ashhalī, the Badrī (البدري), at whose death the Throne shook.
His virtues are well known (المشهور) in the Ṣaḥīḥ collections, in the Sīrah, and elsewhere.
I have cited a portion of that in (Tārīkh al-Islām) , under the year of his death.
Ibn al-Kalbī transmitted: عن عبد الحميد بن أبي عيسى بن جبر، عن أبيه:
That Quraysh heard an unseen voice on Abū Qubays saying:
If they embrace Islam (2) , the two Saʿds, Muḥammad will be ... in Mecca, fearing no opposition from any opponent
Abū Sufyān said: Who are the two Saʿds? Saʿd of Bakr, Saʿd of Tamīm?
Then in the night they heard the unseen voice saying:
O Saʿd, Saʿd of al-Aws, be you a helper ... and O Saʿd, Saʿd of the two Khazraj, the noble chiefs ⟦1:279⟧
Answer the caller to guidance, and set your hope ... upon Allah, in al-Firdaws, with the hope of one who knows
For the reward of Allah to the seeker of guidance ... is gardens of al-Firdaws with fine furnishings
Abū Sufyān said: He is -by Allah- Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, and Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah (1) .
Saʿd ibn Muʿādh embraced Islam at the hands of Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr.
Ibn Isḥāq said: When he embraced Islam he stood before his people and said:
O Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal! How do you regard my standing among you?
They said: Our chief in merit, and the most blessed of us in character.
He said: Then speaking with you is forbidden to me, your men and your women, until you believe in Allah and His Messenger.
He said: By Allah, there did not remain in the quarter of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal a man or a woman but they embraced Islam (2) .
أبو إسحاق: عن عمرو بن ميمون، عن ابن مسعود، قال:
Saʿd ibn Muʿādh set out to perform ʿumrah and stayed with Umayyah ibn Khalaf; whenever Umayyah set out for Syria he would pass by Medina and stay with him.
Umayyah said to him: Wait until, when midday comes and the people are inattentive, you can circumambulate.
While Saʿd was circumambulating, Abū Jahl came to him and said: Who is this circumambulating in safety?
He said: I am Saʿd.
He said: Do you circumambulate in safety, when you have given refuge to Muḥammad and his companions?
He said: Yes.
They quarrelled.
Umayyah said: Do not raise your voice against Abū al-Ḥakam, for he is the chief of the people of the valley.
Saʿd said: By Allah, if you prevent me, I will cut off your trade route to Syria.
He said: Umayyah kept saying: Do not raise your voice.
He grew angry and said: Leave us alone, for I heard Muḥammad ﷺ saying: he claims that he will kill you.
He said: Me?
He said: Yes.
He said: By Allah, Muḥammad does not lie. ⟦1:280⟧
He almost soiled himself (1) , and he returned to his wife and said: Do you know what my Yathribī brother said to me? He claimed that he heard Muḥammad claim that he will kill me.
She said: By Allah, Muḥammad does not lie.
When they went out to Badr, his wife said: Do you not remember what your Yathribī brother said to you?
He wanted not to go out, but Abū Jahl said to him: You are one of the nobles of the people of the valley, so travel with us for a day or two.
He travelled with them, and Allah killed him (2) .
Ibn Shihāb said: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh was present at Badr, and was shot on the day of the Trench; he lived for a month, then his wound reopened, and he died.
Ibn Isḥāq: Abū Laylā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sahl narrated to me:
That ʿĀʾishah was in the fortress of Banū Ḥārithah on the day of the Trench, and the mother of Saʿd was with her. Saʿd passed by wearing a short coat of mail from which his whole forearm protruded, with a spear in his hand which he was brandishing proudly, and he was saying:
Wait a little, and he will witness the battle ... Ḥamal
There is no harm in death ... when the appointed term has come
Meaning: Ḥamal ibn Badr.
His mother said to him: O my son! You have lagged behind.
I said to her: O Umm Saʿd! I wish that Saʿd's coat of mail were more ample than it is.
Saʿd was struck by an arrow that severed his arm vein; Ibn al-ʿAriqah shot him, and when it struck him he said: Take it from me, and I am Ibn al-ʿAriqah.
He said: May Allah make your face sweat in the Fire. O Allah, if You have kept back anything of the war with Quraysh, then keep me alive ⟦1:281⟧ for it, for there is no people I would rather strive against for Your sake than a people who harmed Your Prophet, called him a liar and expelled him. O Allah, if You have brought the war between us and them to an end, then make it a martyrdom for me, and do not let me die until my eye is consoled concerning Banū Qurayẓah (1) .
هشام: عن أبيه، عن عائشة، قالت:
A man of Quraysh called Ḥibbān ibn al-ʿAriqah shot Saʿd, hitting him in the arm vein, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ pitched a tent for him in the mosque so that he could visit him from nearby.
She said: Then his wound dried up and began to heal.
She said: Saʿd supplicated, saying in it: If You have brought the war between us and them to an end, then make it burst open, and make my death in it.
It burst open from his upper chest, and nothing alarmed them but the blood flowing.
They said: O people of the tent! What is this?
And behold, his wound was gushing, and he died of it.
Agreed upon (المتفق عليه) (2) in a longer form than this.
الليث: عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر، قال:
Saʿd was shot on the day of the Confederates, and they severed his arm vein; the Prophet ﷺ cauterised it with fire, and his hand swelled, so he left it, and the blood drained from him, so he cauterised it ⟦1:282⟧ again, and his hand swelled.
When he saw that, he said: O Allah, do not let my soul depart until my eye is consoled concerning Banū Qurayẓah.
His vein held, and not a drop dripped from it until they submitted to the judgement of Saʿd.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent for him, and he judged that their men should be killed, and their women and children taken captive.
He said: They were four hundred, and when he had finished killing them his vein burst open (1) .
يزيد بن عبد الله بن الهاد: عن معاذ بن رفاعة، عن جابر، قال:
The Prophet ﷺ sat at the grave of Saʿd while he was being buried, and said: (Glory be to Allah) twice, and the people glorified Allah.
Then he said: (Allah is greatest, Allah is greatest) , and they declared Allah's greatness.
He said: (I marvel at this righteous servant: he was pressed hard in his grave, until this was when it was eased for him (2)) .
ابن إسحاق: حدثني من لا أتهم، عن الحسن البصري، قال:
Saʿd was corpulent, but when they carried him they found him light.
Some men among the hypocrites said: By Allah, he was ⟦1:283⟧ corpulent, yet we have never carried anyone lighter than him.
That reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: (He has bearers other than you. By the One in whose hand my soul is, the angels rejoiced at the soul of Saʿd, and the Throne shook for him (1)) .
يزيد بن هارون: أنبأنا محمد بن عمرو بن علقمة، عن أبيه، عن جده، عن عائشة، قالت:
I went out on the day of the Trench following the tracks of the people, and I heard the tread of the ground behind me, and there was Saʿd, and with him his nephew al-Ḥārith ibn Aws carrying his shield, so I sat down.
Saʿd passed by wearing a coat of mail from which his limbs protruded, and he was among the tallest and biggest of people. I rushed into a garden, and there was a group of people in it, among them ʿUmar.
He said: What brought you? By Allah, you are bold! What makes you feel safe from a calamity befalling?
He kept blaming me until I wished that the earth would split open at that moment so that I could enter it.
And there was a man wearing a helmet, and he raised it from his face, and behold, it was Ṭalḥah, and he said:
Woe to you! You have said too much. And where is retreat or flight except to Allah? (2)
محمد بن عمرو: عن محمد بن إبراهيم، حدثني علقمة بن وقاص، عن عائشة، قالت:
We came back with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, returning from Mecca, until, when we were at Dhū al-Ḥulayfah, with Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr between me and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he met youths of Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal of the Anṣār.
Usayd asked them, and they announced to him the death of his wife, so he covered his head, weeping.
I said to him: May Allah forgive you! Do you weep over a woman when you are a companion of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah has granted ⟦1:284⟧ you the precedence that He has granted?!
He said: It is right for me not to weep over anyone after Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, when I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say what he said.
He said: I said: And what did you hear?
He said: He said: (The Throne shook at the death of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh (1)) .
Ismāʿīl ibn Muslim al-ʿAbdī: Abū al-Mutawakkil narrated to us:
That the Prophet ﷺ mentioned fever and said: (Whoever has it, it is his share of the Fire) .
Saʿd ibn Muʿādh asked his Lord for it, and it clung to him and did not leave him until he died (2) .
Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, who said:
Saʿd ibn Muʿādh was shot on the day of the Confederates, and they severed his arm vein; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cauterised it with fire, and his hand swelled, and it bled, so he cauterised it again (3) .
Abū Isḥāq, from ʿAmr ibn Shuraḥbīl, who said:
When Saʿd's wound burst open, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ hastened to him and propped him against his chest, with the blood flowing over him.
Abū Bakr came and said: Alas, my back is broken over Saʿd!
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Gently, Abū Bakr) .
ʿUmar came and said: Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we shall return (4) .
Shuʿbah narrated it from him.
محمد بن عمرو: عن أبيه، عن جده، عن عائشة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar attended Saʿd ibn Muʿādh while he was dying in the domed tent that ⟦1:285⟧ the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had pitched for him in the mosque.
She said: By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad, I could distinguish the weeping of Abū Bakr from the weeping of ʿUmar while I was in my chamber; they were as Allah said: “compassionate among themselves” (Qurʾān 48:29) .
ʿAlqamah said: I said: O mother! How did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ act?
She said: His eye would not shed tears for anyone, but when he felt grief, he would simply take hold of his beard (1) .
يزيد بن هارون: أنبأنا إسماعيل بن أبي خالد، عن رجل من الأنصار، قال:
When Saʿd had given judgement concerning Banū Qurayẓah and then returned, his wound burst open. That reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he came to him and placed his head in his lap; he was covered with a white cloth, and he was a fair-skinned, large-bodied man.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (O Allah, Saʿd has striven (2) in Your path, believed Your Messenger, and fulfilled what was due from him, so receive his soul with the best with which You have received a soul) .
When Saʿd heard the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he opened his eyes and said:
Peace be upon you, O Messenger of Allah! I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah.
The Prophet ﷺ said to the people of the house: (As many of His angels as you are in number in the house have asked Allah's permission to attend the death of Saʿd) .
He said: His mother was weeping and saying:
Woe to your mother, Saʿd ... for resolve and earnestness
It was said to her: Do you recite poetry over Saʿd?
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (Leave her, for other poets are greater liars) .
This is mursal (مرسل) (3) .
الواقدي: أنبأنا معاذ بن محمد، عن عطاء بن أبي مسلم، عن عكرمة، عن ⟦1:286⟧ ابن عباس، قال:
When Saʿd's arm burst with blood, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose to him and embraced him, with the blood spattering the face and beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until he passed away (1) .
ʿĀṣim ibn ʿUmar, from Maḥmūd ibn Labīd, who said:
When Saʿd's arm vein was struck and he grew gravely ill, they moved him to a woman called Rufaydah, who treated the wounded.
Whenever the Prophet ﷺ passed by him, he would say: (How are you this evening? And how are you this morning?) .
He would tell him, until the night came in which his people moved him; he had grown gravely ill, and they carried him to Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal, to their dwellings.
The Messenger of Allah came, and it was said: They have gone off with him.
He went out, and we went out with him, and he hurried until the straps of our sandals broke and our cloaks fell off.
His companions complained of that to him, and he said: (I fear that the angels will get to him before us and wash him as they washed Ḥanẓalah) .
He reached the house while he was being washed, and his mother was weeping over him and saying:
Woe to the mother of Saʿd for Saʿd ... for resolve and earnestness
He said: (Every weeping woman lies, except the mother of Saʿd) .
Then he was carried out.
He said: The people said to him: We have never carried a dead man lighter for us than him, O Messenger of Allah.
He said: (What would prevent him from being light, when such-and-such a number of angels have come down who had never come down before their day, and they carried him with you (2)) .
شعبة: عن سماك، سمع عبد الله بن شداد يقول:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered ⟦1:287⟧ upon Saʿd while he was in the throes of death, and said: (May Allah reward you with good as chief of a people, for you have fulfilled what you promised Him, and Allah will surely fulfil for you what He promised you (1)) .
حماد بن سلمة: عن محمد بن زياد، عن عبد الرحمن بن سعد بن معاذ:
That Banū Qurayẓah submitted to the judgement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he sent for Saʿd, who was brought carried on a donkey, worn out by his wound.
He said to him: (Advise me concerning these people) .
He said: I know that Allah has commanded you concerning them with a command that you will carry out.
He said: (Yes, but advise me) .
He said: If I were put in charge of their affair, I would kill their fighting men and take their children captive.
He said: (By the One in whose hand my soul is, you have advised me concerning them with what Allah commanded me (2)) .
محمد بن صالح التمار: عن سعد بن إبراهيم، عن عامر بن سعد، عن أبيه، قال:
When Saʿd judged concerning Banū Qurayẓah that whoever the razors had passed over (3) should be killed:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (He has judged concerning them with the judgement of Allah with which He judged from above the seven ⟦1:288⟧ heavens (1)) .
إسرائيل: عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي ميسرة، قال:
Saʿd's blood did not stop until the Prophet ﷺ took hold of his forearm, and the blood rose to his upper arm; Saʿd was saying: O Allah, do not let me die until You give me satisfaction from Banū Qurayẓah (2) .
الواقدي: حدثني سعيد بن محمد، عن ربيح بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي سعيد، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال:
I was among those who dug Saʿd's grave in al-Baqīʿ, and the scent of musk wafted over us every time we dug, until we reached the niche.
Then Rubayḥ said: وأخبرني محمد بن المنكدر، عن محمد بن شرحبيل بن حسنة، قال:
Someone took a handful of soil from Saʿd's grave and went off with it, then looked, and behold, it was musk (3) .
Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAlqamah narrated it from Ibn al-Munkadir (4) .
الواقدي: أنبأنا عبيد بن جبيرة، عن الحصين بن عبد الرحمن بن عمرو بن سعد بن معاذ، قال:
Saʿd ibn Muʿādh was a fair-skinned man, tall, handsome, with a fine face, large-eyed, with a fine beard. He was shot on the day of the Trench, in the year 5 of ⟦1:289⟧ the Hijrah, and died of that wound, being at that time aged 37; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed over him, and he was buried in al-Baqīʿ (1) .
ابن سعد: أنبأنا محمد بن عمر، حدثني إبراهيم بن الحصين، عن داود بن الحصين، عن عبد الرحمن بن جابر، عن أبيه، قال:
When they reached Saʿd's grave, four men went down into it: al-Ḥārith ibn Aws, Usayd ibn al-Ḥuḍayr, Abū Nāʾilah Silkān, and Salamah ibn Salāmah ibn Waqsh, while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood by.
When he was placed in his grave, the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ changed, and he glorified Allah three times, and the Muslims glorified Allah until al-Baqīʿ shook; then he declared Allah's greatness three times, and the Muslims declared Allah's greatness. He was asked about that.
He said: (The grave became narrow for your companion, and he was squeezed with a squeeze from which, if anyone were to be saved, he would have been saved; then Allah relieved him) (2) .
I say: This squeeze is not in any way part of the punishment of the grave; rather, it is something the believer experiences, just as he experiences the pain of losing his child and his close friend (3) in this world, and as he experiences the pain of his illness, the pain of his soul's departure, the pain of his questioning in his grave and his testing, the pain of being affected by his family's weeping over him, the pain of rising from his grave, the pain of the Standing and its terror, the pain of coming to the Fire, and the like. All these tremors may befall the servant, yet they are not part of the punishment of the grave, nor of the punishment of Hell at all; but Allah is gentle with the God-fearing servant in some or all of that, and there is no rest for the believer short of meeting his Lord.
Allah the Exalted said: “And warn them of the Day of Regret” (Qurʾān 19:39), and He said: “And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts are at the throats” (Qurʾān 40:18) .
So we ask Allah the Exalted for pardon and hidden kindness. Despite these shocks, Saʿd is among those whom we know to be of the people of Paradise, and that he is ⟦1:290⟧ among the highest of the martyrs (may Allah be pleased with him).
It is as though you, O you, think that the one who attains salvation is touched by no terror in the two abodes, nor fright, nor pain, nor fear. Ask your Lord for well-being, and that He gather us in the company of Saʿd.
شعبة: حدثنا سعد بن إبراهيم، عن نافع، عن عائشة:
From the Prophet ﷺ, who said: (The grave has a squeeze, and if anyone were to be saved from it, Saʿd ibn Muʿādh would have been saved from it (1)) .
Its chain of transmission (الإسناد) is strong.
عقبة بن مكرم: حدثنا ابن أبي عدي، عن شعبة، عن سعد بن إبراهيم، عن نافع، عن صفية بنت أبي عبيد، عن عائشة:
From the Prophet ﷺ: (If anyone were saved from the squeeze of the grave, Saʿd would have been saved from it (2)) .
يزيد بن هارون: أنبأنا محمد بن عمرو، عن واقد بن عمرو بن سعد، قال:
I entered upon Anas ibn Mālik - and Wāqid was among the biggest and tallest of people - and he said to me: Who are you?
I said: I am Wāqid ibn ʿAmr ibn Saʿd ibn Muʿādh.
He said: You do resemble Saʿd.
Then he wept, and wept a great deal.
Then he said: May Allah have mercy on Saʿd; he was among the biggest and tallest of people. The Messenger of Allah sent an army to Ukaydir (3) of Dūmah, and he sent to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a robe of brocade woven with gold; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put it on, and they began touching it and looking at it.
He said: (Do you marvel at this robe?) .
They said: O Messenger of Allah! We have never seen ⟦1:291⟧ a garment finer than it.
He said: (By Allah, the handkerchiefs of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh in Paradise are finer than what you see (1)) .
It is said: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh and Asʿad ibn Zurārah were maternal cousins.
Ibn Isḥāq said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ established brotherhood between Saʿd ibn Muʿādh and Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ.
It is also said: he established brotherhood between him and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
The saying of the Prophet ﷺ has been mass-transmitted (المتواتر) (2) : (The Throne shook at the death of Saʿd out of joy at him) .
It is established that the Prophet ﷺ said, concerning a robe whose beauty they marvelled at: (The handkerchiefs of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh in Paradise are better than this (3)) .
Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: حدثنا عوف، عن أبي نضرة، عن أبي سعيد:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The Throne shook at the death of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh) (4) . ⟦1:292⟧
Then al-Naḍr - and he is the Imam (الإمام) of the philologists - said: “shook” means: rejoiced.
الأعمش: عن أبي سفيان، عن جابر مرفوعا: (The Throne of the Most Merciful shook at the death of Saʿd (1)) .
يوسف بن الماجشون: عن أبيه، عن عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة، عن جدته رميثة، قالت:
I heard the Prophet ﷺ say - and had I wished to kiss the seal that was between his shoulders, from my nearness to him, I would have done so - he was saying: (The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for him) .
That is, for Saʿd ibn Muʿādh (2) .
A good chain of transmission (الإسناد).
Al-Nasāʾī recorded by way of معاذ بن رفاعة، عن جابر، قال:
Jibrīl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: Who is this righteous servant who has died? The gates of heaven were opened for him, and the Throne moved for him.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, and behold, it was Saʿd.
He said: He sat at his grave ... the hadith (3) .
إسماعيل بن أبي خالد: عن إسحاق بن راشد، عن أسماء بنت يزيد، قالت:
When Saʿd ibn Muʿādh died, his mother cried out.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (Will your tears not cease, and your grief go? For your son is the first for whom Allah laughed, and the Throne shook for him) . ⟦1:293⟧
This is mursal (مرسل).
ابن جريج: عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر:
That he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say, while Saʿd's bier was before them: (The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for it (1)) .
ابن أبي عروبة: عن قتادة، عن أنس:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, while Saʿd's bier was laid down: (The Throne of the Most Merciful shook for it (2)) .
جماعة: عن عطاء بن السائب، عن مجاهد، عن ابن عمر يرفعه: (The Throne shook out of love for Allah's meeting with Saʿd (3)) .
يونس: عن ابن إسحاق، عن معاذ بن رفاعة، قال:
Whomever you wish of the men of my people narrated to me: that Jibrīl came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when Saʿd passed away, wearing a turban of brocade wound about his head, and said:
O Muḥammad! Who is this dead man for whom the gates of heaven have been opened, and for whom the Throne has shaken?!
He rose quickly, dragging his garment, to Saʿd, and found that he had died (4) .
Ibn Isḥāq said: عن أمية بن عبد الله، عن بعض آل سعد:
That a man said:
The Throne of Allah has not shaken at the death of any perishing one ... we have heard of, except for Saʿd Abū ʿAmr
عبد الله بن إدريس: حدثنا عبيد الله، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر - and some of them ⟦1:294⟧ narrated it as mursal (مرسل) - he said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (This is the righteous servant for whom the Throne moved, the gates of heaven were opened, and seventy thousand angels attended him who had never come down to earth before that; he was squeezed with a squeeze, then it was relieved from him) .
Meaning: Saʿd (1) .
Narrated by: محمد بن سعد، عن إسماعيل بن مسعود، عنه.
Abū Maʿshar, from Saʿīd al-Maqburī:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (If anyone were saved from the pressure of the grave, Saʿd would have been saved; he was squeezed with a squeeze that made his ribs interlock, because of the trace of urine (2)) . This is disconnected (المنقطع).
It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ carried Saʿd's bier for a few steps, but that is not authentic (الصحيح).
الواقدي: حدثني سعيد بن محمد، عن ربيح بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبيه، عن جده أبي سعيد، قال:
I was among those who dug Saʿd's grave in al-Baqīʿ, and the scent of musk wafted over us every time we dug.
Rubayḥ said: فأخبرني محمد بن المنكدر، عن رجل، قال:
Someone took a handful of soil from Saʿd's grave and went off with it, then looked at it afterwards, and behold, it was musk (3) .
Something similar was narrated by: محمد بن عمرو بن علقمة، عن ابن المنكدر، عن محمد بن شرحبيل بن حسنة.
محمد بن عمرو بن علقمة: عن أبيه، عن جده، عن عائشة، قالت: There was no ⟦1:295⟧ one whose loss was harder on the Muslims, after the Prophet ﷺ and his two companions, or one of them, than Saʿd ibn Muʿādh (1) .
لواقدي: أنبأنا عبيد بن جبيرة، عن الحصين بن عبد الرحمن بن عمرو بن سعد بن معاذ، قال:
Saʿd was fair-skinned, tall, handsome, with a fine face, large-eyed, with a fine beard; he lived for 37 years (2) .
أبو إسحاق السبيعي: عن رجل، عن حذيفة:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The Throne shook at the soul of Saʿd ibn Muʿādh (3)) .
Sulaymān al-Taymī narrated from al-Ḥasan:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (The Throne of the Most Merciful shook at the death of Saʿd (4)) .
ابن سعد: أنبأنا محمد بن فضيل، عن عطاء بن السائب، عن مجاهد، عن ابن عمر، قال:
The Throne shook out of love for Allah's meeting with Saʿd.
He said: He only means: the couch.
And he recited: “And he raised his parents upon (5) the throne” [Yūsuf: 100] .
He said: Its planks merely came apart.
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered his grave and was held back there.
When he came out, it was said: O Messenger of Allah! What held you back?
He said: (Saʿd was squeezed in the grave with a squeeze, so I prayed to Allah to remove it from him) (6) . ⟦1:296⟧
I say: As for interpreting it as the couch, I do not know whether it is the saying of Ibn ʿUmar or the saying of Mujāhid. This is an interpretation that serves no purpose, for it has come firmly established as “the Throne of the Most Merciful” and “the Throne of Allah”. The Throne is a created thing of Allah, made subservient; if He wills that it shake, it shakes by the will of Allah, and He placed in it awareness for its love of Saʿd, just as the Exalted placed awareness in the mountain of Uḥud for its love of the Prophet ﷺ.
And the Exalted said: “O mountains, repeat praises with him” [Sabaʾ: 10] .
And He said: “The seven heavens and the earth glorify Him” [al-Isrāʾ: 44] .
Then He made it general, saying: “And there is not a thing but glorifies His praise” (Qurʾān 17:44), and this is the truth.
In (Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī) there is the saying of Ibn Masʿūd: We used to hear the glorification of the food while it was being eaten (1) .
This is a vast subject, whose way is faith.
أبو نعيم: حدثنا إسماعيل بن مسلم العبدي، عن أبي المتوكل:
That the Prophet ﷺ mentioned fever and said: (Whoever has it, it is his share of the Fire) .
Saʿd ibn Muʿādh asked his Lord for it, and it clung to him until he left this world (2) .
Saʿd's children were: ʿAbd Allāh and ʿAmr; and ʿAmr had nine children.
